 CORAM: HONOURABLE MR.JUSTICE G.R.UDHWANI State Of Gujarat - Thro' Yogeshchandra ... vs K P Salim - Partner Of Lucky Restaurant & 7 on 22 September, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156188734/
1  Date : 22/09/2015
ORAL JUDGMENT

The petitioner is aggrieved by the order dated 29/05/2010 passed by the learned  Metropolitan HC-NIC Page 1 of 5 Created On Sat Jun 10 02:26:31 IST 2017 R/CR.RA/609/2010 JUDGMENT Magistrate, Court No.8, Ahmedabad, whereby application Exhibit26 moved by  accused Nos.2 to 9 in Criminal Case No.6106 of 2009 lodged under the Prevention of  F o o d A d u l t e r a t i o n A c t f o r d i s c h a r g e w a s a c c e p t e d u n t i l  the Court records the evidence before framing of the charge i.e. the matter was at a pre charge stage under the relevant provisions of the Code of Criminal  Procedure (for short Cr.PC).
2. Having considered the rival contentions, it is noticed from the impugned order that the  t r i a l C o u r t e x p r e s s e d t w o f o l d o p i n i o n b e i n g ( 0 1 ) t h a t t h e r e  w a s n o m a t e r i a l a g a i n s t a c c u s e d N o s . 2 t o 9 ( 0 2 ) t h a t  the material is yet to be collected before framing of the charge against the said accused.

3. The submission of the learned APP is that the case was instituted otherwise than  on police report and therefore Section 244 of the Cr.PC was applicable and in view of  said provision, after appearance of the accused, the Magistrate is obliged  to proceed to hear the prosecution and take all the evidence as may be produced in support  of the prosecution. It is therefore submitted that no question for discharge of the  accused at that stage arose since concededly the learned Magistrate was yet  t o h e a r t h e p r o s e c u t i o n a n d t a k e a l l t h e e v i d e n c e a s  m a y b e p r o d u c e d i n s u p p o r t o f t h e p r o s e c u t i o n .

I t i s  contended that it was only after the completion of the said procedure that the question of  framing of the charge or discharge of the accused of the charges HC-NIC Page 2 of 5 C r e a t e d O n S a t J u n 1 0 0 2 : 2 6 : 3 1 I S T 2 0 1 7 R / C R . R A / 6 0 9 / 2 0 1 0 J U D G M E N T w o u l d a r i s e .
R e l y i n g u p o n t h e o b s e r v a t i o n s m a d e i n t h e  i m p u g n e d j u d g m e n t a n d o r d e r , i t i s c o n t e n d e d t h a t t h e

Court below was conscious of the said position of law, still however, it fell in error in  discharging the accused until framing of the charge, without even  hearing the case of the prosecution under Section 244 of the Cr.PC.
3.1 Learned APP would contend that a question of discharge will arise for consideration only  a f t e r t a k i n g o f a l l e v i d e n c e r e f e r r e d t o i n S e c t i o n 2 4 4 , a s  provided in Section 245 of Cr.PC and the accused can be discharged at any previous stage, if  for the reasons to be recorded by the Magistrate, he considers the charge to be groundless, as  provided in sub section (2) of Section 245. 
3 . 2 I t i s a r g u e d t h a t u n d e r a n y c a s e , t h e  q u e s t i o n o f d i s c h a r g e c o u l d b e c o n s i d e r e d o n l y a f t e r  State Of Gujarat - Thro' Yogeshchandra ... vs K P Salim - Partner Of Lucky Restaurant & 7 on 22 September, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156188734/
2 c o l l e c t i o n o f e v i d e n c e o r a f t e r t h e c o n c l u s i o n r e a c h e d  b y t h e l e a r n e d M a g i s t r a t e t h a t t h e c h a r g e , i f f r a m e d  would be groundless.

It is argued that in the instant case, the right of the prosecution to  p r o d u c e t h e e v i d e n c e u n d e r s u b s e c t i o n ( 1 ) o f S e c t i o n 2 4 4 w a s y e t  to be exhausted and the trial Court committed an error in discharging the accused and that  too until collection of evidence.
It was argued that such a procedure or such an  order of discharge is not contemplated anywhere in Section 245 of the Cr.PC.
HC-NIC Page 3 of 5 Created On Sat Jun 10 02:26:31 IST
R/CR.RA/609/2010 JUDGMENT 4.
Learned Counsel for the respondent supported the impugned judgment and order with the
s u b m i s s i o n t h a t i t w a s w i t h i n t h e j u r i s d i c t i o n o f t h e l e a r n e d
M a g i s t r a t e t o d i s c h a r g e t h e a c c u s e d u n t i l t h e m a t e r i a l  is brought on record.
It is therefore urged that this Court may not interfere in its revisional  jurisdiction.
5 . F r o m t h e s u b m i s s i o n s m a d e a n d t h e i m p u g n e d  o r d e r , i t i s c l e a r t h a t t h e r e w a s n o o c c a s i o n o r s t a g e

o f c o n s i d e r i n g t h e a p p l i c a t i o n f o r d i s c h a r g e a n d t h e  matter was being considered under Section 244 of the Cr.PC wherefrom it is very clear that  the learned Magistrate was first required to collect the material as may be produced by the  prosecution.
The order deferring the collection of material or evidence and discharging the  accused until then was absolutely contrary to Section 244 of the Cr.PC.
The impugned  order therefore cannot be sustained.
6. It is very clear from Section 245 of the Cr.PC that for the purpose of considering
t h e a p p l i c a t i o n f o r d i s c h a r g e o f t h e a c c u s e d , t h e

M a g i s t r a t e i s r e q u i r e d t o c o m e t o t h e c o n c l u s i o n t h a t  o n t h e b a s i s o f t h e e v i d e n c e c o l l e c t e d u n d e r S e c t i o n  2 4 5 , t h a t n o c a s e a g a i n s t t h e a c c u s e d h a s b e e n m a d e  o u t w h i c h , i f u n r e b u t t e d w o u l d w a r r a n t h i s c o n v i c t i o n .

The second contingency of discharging the accused is that of the charge being groundless as  p r o v i d e d i n s u b s e c t i o n ( 2 ) o f S e c t i o n 2 4 5 . T h a t p o w e r c a n b e  exercised even at any previous stage of the case.

Further, the procedure under Section 245 do not provide for "interim discharge" i.e.
 discharge until the collection of evidence under Section 244 of Cr.PC.
7 .
I n t h e r e s u l t , t h e i m p u g n e d o r d e r i s q u a s h e d
a n d s e t a s i d e .
T h e m a t t e r i s r e m a n d e d t o t h e l e a r n e d  Metropolitan Magistrate, Ahmedabad with a direction to proceed in accordance with law.
8. Rule is made absolute to the aforesaid extent.
No costs.

9 . T h e m a t t e r w a s p e n d i n g s i n c e 2 0 0 9 a n d i s  o n l y a t p r e l i m i n a r y s t a g e , t h e r e f o r e t h e t r i a l C o u r t  i s d i r e c t e d t o d e c i d e t h e m a t t e r w i t h i n a p e r i o d o f  six months from the date of the receipt of the writ of this Court.
